translations.text: What further blow are you adding to your lawlessness? Every head is distressed, and every heart is sorrowful.
Again, [?] the abundance of your sacrifices to me, says the Lord. I am full of burnt offerings of rams and the fat of lambs, and I do not want the blood of calves and goats.
Your rulers are disobedient, partners of thieves. They love gifts and pursue rewards. They do not give justice to orphans, and they pay no attention to the widow’s case.
For the day of the Lord of Hosts is coming upon everyone who is insolent and proud, and upon everyone who is exalted and lofty, and they will be humbled.
Every person will be humbled, human pride will fall, and the Lord alone will be exalted on that day.
I will make children their rulers, and mockers will lord it over them.
On that day he will answer and say, “I will not be your leader, for there is neither bread nor clothing in my house. I will not be the leader of this people.”
They say, “Let us bind the righteous man, because he is troublesome to us.” So now they will eat the fruits of the works of their hands.
He will be shade from the heat, a shelter, and a refuge from storm and rain.
What more shall I do for my vineyard that I have not done for it? I waited for it to produce grapes, but it produced thorns.

For the vineyard of the Lord of Hosts is the house of Israel, and the people of Judah are the beloved new planting. I waited for it to bring about justice, but it brought about lawlessness; not righteousness, but an outcry.
They will not hunger or grow weary. They will not doze or sleep. They will not loosen the belts around their waists, and the straps of their sandals will not break.
After these things the Lord will send the people far away, and those who remain will multiply on the earth.
Or the evil person will abandon wickedness to choose what is good for himself. They will abandon the land that you fear, so that you will not take it in distress before the two kings.
On that day the Lord will shave with the great drunken razor the head of the king of the Assyrians beside the river, along with the hair of his feet, and he will remove his beard.
The Lord said to me, “Take a large scroll of new papyrus and write on it in ordinary human writing: ‘Carry out the plundering of the spoils quickly, for it has drawn near.’”

If you trust in him, he will be a means of purification for you, and you will not stumble against him as against a stumbling stone or a rock that causes a fall. But the house of Jacob is in a trap, and those living in Jerusalem are in a [?].

For a little child has been born to you; a son has been given to you. His authority rests on his shoulder, and his name will be called “Messenger of the Great Counsel.” For I will bring peace upon the rulers, and salvation to him.
The Lord sent a word against Jacob, and it came upon Israel.
The bricks have fallen, but come, let us cut stones, cut down sycamores and cedars, and build ourselves a tower.

Therefore God will not rejoice over their young people, nor will he have mercy on their orphans and widows, because they are all lawless and wicked, and every mouth speaks unjustly. Despite all these things, his anger has not turned away, but his hand is still raised.

Therefore this is what the Lord of Hosts says: “My people who live in Zion, do not be afraid of the Assyrians, for he will strike you with a rod. For I will bring a blow upon you so that you see the road to Egypt.”
God will bring upon them a blow like the blow he brought upon Midian in a place of distress, and his anger upon the road beside the sea, the road that leads to Egypt.
On that day the fear of him will be removed from you, and the yoke from your neck; the yoke will be destroyed and removed from your necks.

But he will judge the case of the humble and rebuke the proud. He will save the humble of the earth and strike the earth with the word of his mouth, and with the breath from his lips he will destroy the ungodly person.

And the Lord will turn the sea of Egypt into a desert, and he will bring his hand against the river with a violent wind. He will strike the seven valleys of Egypt, so that people can walk through them in sandals.
And he will say on that day, “I will praise you, Lord, because you were angry with me, but you turned your anger away from me and had mercy on me.”
Raise a signal on an open mountain. Raise your voices; do not be afraid. Beckon with your hands. Open up, rulers!

I am the one who will give the command, and I am the one who will bring them; they are purified. And I am the one who will bring them. Giants are coming against you in my anger, rejoicing and mocking together.
For the stars of heaven, Orion, and all the heavenly array will not give their light. They will grow dark while the sun is out, and the moon will not give its light.
And the Lord will have mercy on Jacob and choose Israel again. They will rest on their own land, and the foreigner will run to them and join the house of Jacob.
And the trees of Lebanon rejoiced over you, along with the cedar of Lebanon: “Since you lay down, the one who cuts us down has not risen.”
Sorrow upon you! For Dibon will be destroyed, the place where your altars are. You will go there to weep. Cry out over Nebo in the land of Moab, for every head will be bald and every arm cut.
The water of Nimrim will dry up, and its grass will wither, for from now on no grass will be green.
For my cry has reached the border of Moab, as far as Eglaim, and its cry as far as the well of Elim.
And you will be put to shame, because Moab has worn himself out at his altars. He will enter his handmade shrines to pray, but they will not be able to save him.
This is the word that the Lord spoke against Moab, just as he said it.
But you will go astray on the day when you plant it. If you sow it in the morning, it will bring its harvest to an end on the day when it comes to an end, and as a father divides among his children.
My heart went astray, and my lawlessness overwhelmed me. My soul fell into terror.
And the remaining strong bows of the descendants of Kedar will become fewer, because the Lord, the God of Israel, has spoken.
The vision concerning the valley of Zion. What has happened to you, that now you have all gone up onto empty rooftops?
Look! The Lord God will cast out and crush the man, and he will take away your robe and your glorious crown.
And everyone honored in his father’s house will trust in him, from the least to the greatest, and they will hang upon him.
Was this not your arrogance from the beginning, before it was handed over?
Take a harp and go around the city, forgotten prostitute. Play the harp well; sing a great deal, so that they may be remembered.
Therefore the curse will devour the earth, because those who live in it have mourned. Therefore those who live on the earth will become poor, and few people will remain.
The brickwork will dissolve and the wall will fall, because the Lord will reign in Zion and in Jerusalem and receive glory before the elders.
Like fainthearted people who thirst in Zion because of the wicked and ungodly people into whose hands you handed us.
For they have put their hope in you, Lord, forever, the great God forever.

For the ungodly person has withered, along with everyone who does not learn to practice righteousness on earth and act truthfully. Let the ungodly person be taken away, so that he will not see the glory of God.
But the dead will not see life, and the physicians will not rise. Therefore you brought disaster upon them and destroyed them, and you removed every male of theirs.
Add evils to them, Lord; add evil to all the honored people of the earth.
Just as he himself struck, will they wound him in the same way? And just as he killed, will they kill him in the same way?
And on that day the Lord will cause turmoil from the channel of the river as far as Rhinocorura. But you, gather the children of Israel one by one.
And the flower that has fallen from the hope of glory on the summit of the high mountain will be like an early fig: whoever sees it wants to swallow it before taking it in his hand.

For these are going astray through wine; they have gone astray because of strong drink. The priest and the prophet have staggered because of wine. They have been shaken by the stupor of strong drink and have gone astray—that is, a dream.
Therefore, look, I will once again change this people, and I will change them. I will destroy the wisdom of the wise and hide the understanding of the intelligent.
For Pharaoh’s shadow will become a shame to you and a disgrace to those who put their trust in Egypt.
And the Lord will give you bread of affliction and troubled water. Those who lead you astray will no longer approach you, for your eyes will see those who lead you astray.

And God will make them hear the glory of his voice. He will reveal the anger of his arm and strike them violently, with furious anger and a consuming flame of wrath, and like water and hail coming down together with violence.

Woe to those who go down to Egypt for help, who put their trust in horses and chariots, for they are numerous, and in the horses, which are exceedingly many. They did not believe in the Holy One of Israel and did not seek God.
And you who devise secret and lawless counsel.
And they will no longer trust in a human being, but they will turn their ears to listen.
Until a spirit comes upon you from on high, and Carmel becomes a wilderness, and Carmel is considered a woodland.
The Lord’s sword is drenched in blood; it has grown fat from the fat of lambs and the fat of goats and rams. For the Lord’s sacrifice is in Bozrah, and there is a great slaughter in Edom.
For the Lord’s day of judgment and the year of repayment for Zion have drawn near upon them.
Then the eyes of the blind will open, and the ears of the deaf will hear.
And in the fourteenth year of Hezekiah’s reign, Sennacherib, king of the Assyrians, came up against the fortified cities of Judea and captured them.

And Isaiah said to them, “This is what you are to say to your master: ‘This is what the Lord says: Do not be afraid of the words you have heard, with which the messengers of the king of the Assyrians have insulted me.’”
This is what you are to say to Hezekiah, king of Judea: “Do not let your God, in whom you trust, deceive you when you say, ‘Jerusalem will not be handed over to the king of the Assyrians.’”
And Hezekiah received the letter from the messengers and opened the letter before the Lord.
Lord of hosts, God of Israel, who sits enthroned upon the cherubim, you alone are God and Lord of all the kingdoms of the inhabited world. You made heaven and earth.

Look, days are coming when they will take everything in your house, together with everything your ancestors have gathered until this day, and carry it to Babylon. They will leave nothing behind. God has said this.
Do you not know? Do you not hear? Were you not told from the beginning? Have you not understood the foundations of the earth?
He who gives strength to the hungry and sorrow to those who are not distressed.
But you, Israel, my servant, Jacob, whom I have chosen, the offspring of Abraham, whom I loved.
And who are blind except my servants, and deaf except those who rule over them? And the servants of God have become blind.
The Lord God decided that he would give honor and exalt a blessing. And I saw.
I will say to the north, “Bring them,” and to the west, “Do not hold them back. Bring my sons from the distant land and my daughters from the end of the earth.”

Be witnesses for me, and I am the witness, says God, along with my son whom I have chosen, so that you may know, understand, and believe that I am God. No other god came into being before me, and there is none after me.
My chosen people, whom I brought into being to proclaim my virtues.
But now listen, Jacob my servant, Israel, whom I have chosen.
He made the rest into a god, a handmade idol, and bowed down to it and prayed to it, saying, “Save me, because you are my god.”
They did not understand how to be wise, because they became blind, unable to see with their eyes or understand with their hearts.
So that those in the places where the sun rises and those in the places where it sets may know that there is none besides me.

This is what the Lord of Hosts says: The labor of Egypt and the trade of the Ethiopians, and the Sabeans, tall men, are coming to you. They will become your servants and follow you, bound with bronze chains on their hands. They will bow down to you and pray to you, saying, “God is in you, and there is no other god besides you.”
For you are God, and we did not know it, the God of Israel, the Savior.

This is what the Lord says, the one who made heaven—he is God—the one who prepared the earth and made it. He is the one who spread it out. He did not make it for emptiness, but for people to live in it: “I am he, I am he, and there is no other besides me.”
Turn to me so that you may live, you who are at the ends of the earth, says the Lord. I am God, and there is no other.

Until their old age, I am he, and until you grow old, I am still he. I am the one who sustains you. I am the one who made you, and I am also the one who will release you. I am the one who will take you to myself and rescue you.
To whom have you compared me? Look and think, you who go astray.
The one who calls a bird from the east and from a distant land concerning the things I have planned. I spoke and brought him; I created him and made him. I brought him and made his path straight.
Sit in grief; go into the darkness, daughter of the Chaldeans. From now on they will no longer call you the power of the kingdom.

And he said to me, “It is a great thing for you to be called my servant, to establish the tribes of Jacob for me and to bring back the scattered people of Israel. Look, I have made you a covenant for a people, a light for the nations, so that you may bring salvation to the end of the earth.”
Saying to those in chains, “Come out,” and to those in darkness, “Show yourselves.” They will be pastured along all their roads, and their pasture will be in every place where people walk.
For the children you lost will say in your ears, “The place is too cramped for me. Make room for me so that I can live here.”
This is what the Lord said: If someone takes a giant captive, he will take spoils, and whoever takes spoils from a mighty man will be saved. But I will judge their case, and I will save my children.

This is what the Lord says: Where is your mother’s certificate of divorce by which I sent her away? Or to which creditor did I sell you? Look, I sold you because of your sins, and because of your lawless acts I sent your mother away.
Listen, listen, my people, and you kings, pay attention to me, because a law is coming from me, and my judgment will be a light for the nations.
And there was no one to comfort you among all your children whom you bore, and there was no one to take your hand among all your children whom you raised.
These two things confront you. Who will grieve with you? Ruin and destruction, famine and the sword. Who will comfort you?
Shake off the dust, rise up and sit down, Jerusalem. Release the bonds around your neck, captive daughter of Zion.
For you will not come out in turmoil, nor will you travel in flight. For the Lord will go before you, and the one who gathers you together is the Lord, the God of Israel.
The Lord did not call you as a wife who has been cast out and is disheartened, nor as a wife hated since her youth, says your God.
But just as heaven is far from the earth, so my way is far from your way, and your thoughts from my thoughts.
For you will come out with gladness, and you will be led with joy. For the mountains and hills will leap, looking toward you with joy, and all the trees of the field will clap their branches.
This is what the Lord says: Maintain justice and practice righteousness, for my salvation is near to coming, and my mercy is near to being revealed.
The Lord who gathers the scattered people of Israel says, “I will gather a congregation to him.”
Your bed is on a high and lofty mountain, and you offered a sacrifice there.
I will not punish you forever, nor will I always be angry with you. For a spirit comes out from me, and I am the one who made every breath.
But the sea will toss the oppressors about like this, and they will be unable to rest.
Share your bread with the hungry, and bring the poor who have no home into your house. If you see someone naked, clothe them, and do not neglect the members of your own family.

They will grope along the wall like a blind person, and they will fumble like those who have no eyes. They will fall at noon like those in the middle of the night. Like those about to die, they will groan.
We have acted unjustly and lied, and we have stopped following God. We have spoken unjust things and disobeyed. We have conceived and pondered words of injustice in our hearts.
They have taken away the truth, and he turned his mind away from understanding. The Lord saw it, and it did not please him, because there was no justice.
Kings will walk in your light, and nations in your brightness.
Strangers will come and tend your sheep, and foreigners will be your farmers and vine growers.
But those who gather them will eat them and bless the Lord, and those who gather them will drink them and eat them in my holy courts.
For you are our Father, because Abraham did not know us, and Israel did not recognize us. But you, Lord, are our Father. Save us; from the beginning your name has been upon us.
No one calls on your name or remembers to take hold of you, for you have turned your face away from us and handed us over because of our sins.
They sleep in tombs and graves to have dreams. They eat pork and broth from sacrifices. All their vessels are polluted.

This is what the Lord says: Just as a grape is found in its cluster, and people say, “Do not destroy it, because the Lord’s blessing is in it,” so I will act for the sake of those who are my servants. For this reason I will not destroy them all.
For heaven and earth will become new, and people will not remember the former things, nor will they come to mind.
They will go out and see the corpses of the people who rebelled against me. For their worm will not die, and their fire will not be extinguished, and all people will look at them.
